# Best Folding Treadmill for Small Spaces (2026): 7 Things to Measure Before You Buy


Last updated November 2026


Folded, the Podium shrinks from 80 inches long to a 49-inch footprint.


**Short answer:** The best folding treadmill for a small space is one that still fits your room when it's open and running. Plan on about 11 by 7 feet of clear floor during workouts and about 4.5 by 3 feet in storage. For walking and jogging in tight rooms, the Aviron Justice is 34 inches wide and folds to a 53-inch footprint. Runners should look at the Aviron Podium, which adds a 4.5 CHP motor and 14 mph and folds even shorter, to 49 inches.


A folding treadmill solves half of the small-space problem. It's compact when you're done, but while you're using it, it's a full-size machine. As[Garage Gym Reviews](https://www.garagegymreviews.com/best-folding-treadmill) puts it, "when unfurled, a folding treadmill can be nearly the same size as a standard treadmill."


One catch never makes the spec sheet: a folded treadmill is out of sight, and out of sight is how a good treadmill becomes an expensive clothes rack by month two.


Grab a tape measure: these seven numbers decide whether a folding treadmill works in your space. (Full disclosure: Aviron makes the Justice, Podium and Summit.)


## In this article


- 1. How much floor does it take while you're using it?
- 2. How much clearance do you need around a treadmill?
- 3. How small does it get when folded?
- 4. Will it fit through the door and under the ceiling?
- 5. Is the deck long and wide enough?
- 6. How much motor and speed do you need?
- 7. How loud will it be?

## 1. How Much Floor Does It Take While You're Using It?


Start with the in-use footprint, because that's the room you need. Both Aviron folders are 80 inches (6 feet 8 inches) long when open. The Justice is 34 inches wide and the Podium 37.


Be honest about how often you'll fold it, too. If the answer is "basically never," consider the non-folding Aviron Summit: at 67 inches long, it's 13 inches shorter in use than either folder.


The Justice in use: 80 inches long, 34 inches wide and 66 inches tall.


## 2. How Much Clearance Do You Need Around a Treadmill?


Aviron recommends at least 24 inches of clear space on all four sides of its treadmills, so you can step on and off safely.[Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/a36384002/best-folding-treadmills-for-runners/) gives the same advice: "at least 2 feet of clearance surrounding your treadmill in every direction while you're running."


Add that to the machine and here's the real floor plan:


- **Justice:** about 10 feet 8 inches by 6 feet 10 inches
- **Podium:** about 10 feet 8 inches by 7 feet 1 inch


Tape that rectangle on the floor with painter's tape before you buy. If something has to sit close, keep it to the sides. Behind the belt is where you'd land if you slipped.


## 3. How Small Does It Get When Folded?


Look for a fold that gives you real floor back. Runner's World warns that plenty of treadmills "technically have a folding mechanism but are not all that much smaller in their folded form."


Folded, the Justice measures 53 by 34 inches and the Podium 49 by 37 inches, both 68 inches tall. That's almost the same floor area, about 12.5 square feet each, and a third to 40% less than when they're open.


Then check how it folds. Garage Gym Reviews notes that a deck without a gas shock "will instead slam to the ground when released," so "watch out for little hands, paws, and your own feet." Both Aviron folders use SafeLift, a pneumatic assist that helps you lift the deck with one hand and lowers it gently on its own. Two transport wheels near the center of gravity let you roll it against a wall.


SafeLift takes most of the weight, so folding the Justice is a one-hand job.


## 4. Will It Fit Through the Door and Under the Ceiling?


Measure the path into the room as well. At 34 inches wide, the Justice fits through a standard 36-inch doorway, so you can move it between rooms or down to the basement without taking it apart. The Podium is 37 inches wide, so check the narrowest door, hallway turn or stairwell on its route.


Folded, both machines stand 68 inches tall (5 feet 8 inches). Check the storage spot for a sloped ceiling or a low shelf.


Incline lifts you, so check the ceiling too. Aviron's rule for the 42% Summit is your height plus 30 inches, and the Justice (15%) and Podium (18%) lift you far less. If you're tall and training under a low basement beam, measure to the lowest point above the belt first.

## 5. Is the Deck Long and Wide Enough?


A small treadmill shouldn't mean a small stride. Garage Gym Reviews suggests a deck "that exceeds 55 inches long and 20 inches wide" if you plan to run or sprint. Walking pads usually fall well short of that, with belts around 15 to 17 inches wide.


The Justice's 20" x 59" deck is rated for users up to 6'6". The Podium's 22" x 60" deck is rated up to 6'7" and gives you two extra inches of width, which helps if you have a wide stride or drift when you're tired. Both decks are cushioned with 8 shock absorbers to take some of the pounding off your knees.


## 6. How Much Motor and Speed Do You Need?


Garage Gym Reviews says 2.0 to 2.5 continuous horsepower (CHP) is enough for power walking with the odd jog, and that serious runners should look for more than 2.5. CHP is what a motor can sustain for a whole session rather than its peak, so it's the number to compare.


The Justice runs a 3.5 CHP brushless motor up to 12.5 mph and a 15% incline, plenty for walking, jogging and regular runs. If you run most days, love intervals or share the belt with other runners, the Podium steps up to 4.5 CHP, 14 mph and an 18% incline.


Check the outlet, too. The Justice's manual calls for a dedicated 110-volt, 15-amp outlet, so the power strip behind the TV won't do.


The Podium has the motor and deck width runners want, and it still folds. For runners

## 7. How Loud Will It Be?


In an apartment, noise is a measurement too. Aviron's treadmills use brushless motors that run at roughly 40 dB at walking speeds, about the background noise of an average home, and around 70 dB at top speed, which is comparable to office noise.


What the downstairs neighbors usually hear is your feet. Put a mat under the machine and save the sprints for daytime. Given the choice, a ground-floor room beats one above a neighbor's bedroom.

## Why Do Folding Treadmills Get Forgotten?


Plenty of home treadmills get abandoned around month two, when the novelty wears off and a workout that feels like a chore loses to the couch. That's the motivation cliff, and a folding treadmill makes it easier to fall off, because once it's tucked against the wall you don't even have to look at it.


Willpower gets the blame, but treadmills were engineered to be boring while the phone in your pocket was engineered to be hard to put down. Aviron put that same game psychology into the treadmill.[Aviron World](https://www.avironactive.com/workouts/) adds points, streaks, levels and live competition to every workout, whether it's a coached class, a scenic route, a game or your own Netflix queue. You can even race-walk 20 kilometers against Daniel Pintado's gold-medal pace from the 2024 Paris Olympics, which works out to 9.4 mph (good luck).


Race-walking an Olympic champion's pace on the treadmill screen: 9.4 mph for 20 kilometers.


In a small space, a folding treadmill has to earn its floor time by being something you want to unfold. Workouts that pull you back are a big part of why **92% of Aviron members are still working out a year later** .

**Our verdict:** For most small spaces, the Aviron Justice is the best folding treadmill. It's the narrowest, it clears a standard doorway and it folds upright to a 53-inch footprint. If you're a runner, get the Podium, which folds even shorter and gives you a bigger motor and deck. Both come with a 30-day risk-free home trial, so you can test the fit in your own room.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Are folding treadmills worth it?


Yes, if you'll fold it at least some of the time or need the floor back between workouts. Folding used to mean flimsy, but many current folders use the same kind of motors and decks as non-folding treadmills. If you know you'll never fold it, put the money toward a machine you'll leave set up.


### Can you run on a folding treadmill?


Yes, as long as the deck and motor are built for it. Look for a deck at least 55 inches long and 20 inches wide and a motor above 2.5 CHP. The Justice (3.5 CHP, 20" x 59") handles regular runs, and the Podium (4.5 CHP, 22" x 60", 14 mph) is built for daily running.


### How much space do you need for a treadmill?


A typical home treadmill is about 6 feet long and 3 feet wide. Add 2 feet of clearance on every side and you need roughly 10 by 7 feet of open floor while you work out, a little more for longer machines like Aviron's 80-inch folders. Folded, the Justice and Podium each take about 12.5 square feet.


### Can you use a folding treadmill in an apartment?


Yes. Choose a brushless motor, which runs quieter, put a mat underneath to protect the floor and keep the machine from shifting, and plug it into its own outlet. Walking is much easier on the neighbors than running, so save sprints for the daytime. Aviron's treadmills run at roughly 40 dB at walking speeds.


### What are the downsides of a folding treadmill?


They're still full-size when they're open, so you need the in-use space either way. Cheaper folders save space by shrinking the motor and deck. Good ones are heavy, so a lift assist and wheels matter. And a folded treadmill is easy to forget about, so pick one you'll want to unfold.


### Can you store a folding treadmill against a wall?


Yes. The Justice and Podium fold the deck up toward the console and stand 68 inches tall, and their transport wheels let you tuck them against a wall. Just make sure the spot doesn't block a vent or an outlet you need.


Make room for a workout you'll actually unfold.


The Justice folds to a 53-inch footprint, with games, classes and scenic routes that give you a reason to open it back up.
